newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht seen fragile despite intervention.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht seen fragile despite intervention.

text.p: The Thai baht is likely to hit new lows in coming months despite the Bank of Thailand's insistence that the currency has sunk far enough, analysts said on Monday.

The central bank's vow on Monday to support the baht would not be enough to withstand an erosion of foreign investor confidence in regional currencies following the de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso and the Thai baht in recent weeks, analysts said.

"The baht will remain fragile in the short term. It's largely due to uncertainty across the region as a lot of people are taking (funds) out of the region," Jimmy Koh at Singapore-based research house I.D.E.A. told Reuters.
"By the end of this year, I expect the baht to be around 31-32 to the dollar," Koh said.
Thailand's worst economic downturn in over a decade and near crisis in the finance sector would add pressure on the currency, analysts said.
"It will take time for the economy to pick up and the financial crisis to be resolved. In the short term, the pressure on the baht will still persist," said Ali Seng at MMS International.
Seng said the baht was expected to fall to about 31-33 baht per dollar by the end of this year, echoing expectations of a number of other analysts.
Analysts said there were also worries about the quality of assets owned by financial institutions after the baht's de facto devaluation and their overexposure to cash-strapped property firms.
Deputy Bank of Thailand Governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawasdi said on Monday he believed the baht's current level of 30 to the dollar was low enough.
The central bank would take action to stabilise the currency and stop more wild fluctuations, he added.
"It is our direct responsibility to take measures to do anything that will help stabilise the foreign exchange rate and ease volatility in the market," he said.
Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond on Monday confirmed the bank had intervened to stem the baht's slide against the U.S. dollar.
"We intervened in the market, but in a very small way. This caused the baht to stabilise in the afternoon," Rerngchai told reporters.
This is the first time since the adoption of the managed float foreign exchange system for the baht on July 2 that the central bank has intervened to defend the currency.
Dealers said the Bank of Thailand, via a small local bank, intervened in the domestic market and sold dollars at the record low level of 30.75-30.80 per dollar.
The baht was quoted at a record low of around 30.30/30.80 per dollar early on Monday in the domestic market compared with 30.00/30.60 late on Friday.
After the central bank's intervention and statement, the baht recovered significantly to trade at around 29.70/30.20 in late afternoon.
